# **Hybrid System One and LLM Control Plane Architecture for an Air-Gapped ESP32-P4 Rust Bitcoin Blake2b Hardware Wallet**

## **Architectural Synergy: High-Impact Jev Control Plane Integrations and the ESP32-P4 Security Boundary**

Integrating TypeSafe's flagship System One model, **Jev** (jev-1.14, accessed via POST /v1/systemone), alongside a System Two reasoning Large Language Model (LLM) inside the GitHub control plane enables deterministic enforcement of cryptographic and silicon-level invariants for an air-gapped, stateless-first (and optionally stateful) Rust Bitcoin and Blake2b hardware wallet targeting the Espressif ESP32-P41. Rather than wasting engineering cycles on low-value control plane automations such as conversational pull request summaries, commit-message style grading, or automated issue labeling, high-assurance firmware development requires focusing exclusively on the three highest-impact integrations: a **Speculative Fan-Out PR Gatekeeper** for stateless memory isolation and constant-time Rust cryptography, an **Atomic Decomposition and Composite Scoring Engine** for eFuse and flash encryption configuration files, and a **Multimodal esp-emulator Verification Pipeline** for optical air-gap framebuffer integrity and post-reset memory residue auditing2.  
The ESP32-P4 System-on-Chip (SoC) provides an exceptional hardware foundation for an air-gapped signing device because it physically omits integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth/BLE radios while pairing a 400 MHz dual-core 32-bit RISC-V High-Performance (HP) processor and a 40 MHz single-core 32-bit RISC-V Low-Power (LP) co-processor with native MIPI-CSI camera and MIPI-DSI display interfaces for optical QR transaction transport4. Its internal memory hierarchy and security peripherals—comprising 8 KB of system Scratchpad Memory (SPM), 768 KB of HP L2MEM, 32 KB of LP SRAM, a 1024-bit one-time programmable (OTP) eFuse controller, hardware XTS-AES-256 flash encryption, Physical Memory Protection (PMP) / Permission Control (PMS), and hardware SHA/ECC/HMAC/DS accelerators—only guarantee key isolation if the firmware and build configuration never violate hardware boundaries4. Crucially, because the ESP32-P4 hardware hash accelerator natively supports SHA-1, SHA-224, and SHA-256 while its hardware ECC/ECDSA engine targets NIST P-256 and P-384 curves, both Bitcoin's secp256k1 signing and Blake2b state commitment and key-derivation hashing must execute in constant-time Rust on the RISC-V cores while binding securely to the hardware True Random Number Generator (TRNG) and Key Management Unit4.  
Relying solely on generative System Two LLMs in continuous integration (CI) pipelines to police these invariants introduces severe operational bottlenecks, including high latency, unpredictable token costs, stochastic prose outputs, and uncalibrated overconfidence1. Jev solves this control plane bottleneck by operating as a fast (\~100 ms), self-consistent System One model trained via Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) to evaluate structured state inputs against narrow, typed questions (Noul, Choice, and Score primitives) in parallel1. Because Jev never generates prose or chooses its own next action, deterministic Python and Rust control plane scripts remain strictly in control—using Jev's calibrated probabilities and confidence scores to auto-approve safe commits, hard-block clear violations, and escalate only ambiguous or high-entropy cryptographic changes to an expensive System Two reasoning LLM1.

## **Interactive Workbench: Speculative Fan-Out, Score Calibration, and Confidence-Gated Routing Mechanics**

To deploy Jev effectively in a security-critical repository, it is essential to understand how System One primitives separate **expected risk (or score)** from **model confidence**, and how custom code combines these independent outputs. Unlike a generative LLM that produces a single autoregressive token stream where earlier tokens bias subsequent judgments, Jev evaluates every question in a POST /v1/systemone request independently and in parallel, ensuring that one primitive's answer never becomes hidden context that alters another primitive's probability distribution.  
![A diagram illustrating how System One primitives evaluate inputs in parallel without sequential token bias, unlike autoregressive LLMs. On the left, a single POST /v1/systemone API request payload containing the document context branches into three parallel evaluation streams simultaneously: Noul Primitive (Binary evaluation yielding probability n in \[0, 1\]), Choice Primitive (Multiclass evaluation yielding probability distribution P and confidence C), and Score Primitive (Rubric evaluation yielding level probabilities P(i), expected score, and confidence C). All three outputs converge into a single structured JSON response body on the right, highlighting that evaluation occurs concurrently and independently in \~100ms.][image2]  
Within this parallel evaluation model, the three core primitives fulfill distinct mathematical functions across the control plane. A **Noul (type: "noul")** evaluates a single binary yes/no proposition and returns a single floating-point number noul ![][image3] representing the calibrated probability that the answer is yes15. Because a Noul has only two outcomes, it carries no separate confidence field; values near 1.0 represent a high-certainty yes, values near 0.0 represent a high-certainty no, and values near 0.5 indicate that the model assigns roughly equal probability to both outcomes15. Conversely, a **Choice (type: "choice")** selects one option from an unordered, mutually exclusive set defined in criteria, returning the winning choice string, the full probabilities distribution across all options summing to 1.0, and a confidence metric ![][image3] computed from how sharply peaked that probability distribution is18. Finally, a **Score (type: "score")** evaluates the state against an ordered rubric of descriptive levels ![][image4] (supporting 2 to 10 levels) and returns a probability ![][image5] for each level ![][image6], a legend mapping level numbers back to rubric descriptions, a continuous score computed as the probability-weighted mean across levels:  
![][image7]  
and a confidence value ![][image3] measuring how tightly the probability mass concentrates on a single level17. Crucially, different probability distributions can yield the exact same score while communicating vastly different risk profiles: on a 3-level cryptographic severity rubric (![][image8]), a distribution of ![][image9] produces a score of ![][image10] with confidence \= 1.0, whereas a bimodal split between completely safe and critically vulnerable (![][image11]) also produces a score of ![][image10], but exhibits low confidence due to the spread across levels17. Inspecting probabilities and confidence alongside score is therefore mandatory to prevent bimodal ambiguity from passing silently through CI gates17.  
![][image12]  
The mathematical dynamics demonstrated in the workbench reveal why combining **Speculative Fan-Out** with **Confidence-Gated Routing** yields an optimal hybrid control plane9. Rather than executing sequential API round-trips—first asking Jev to classify which ESP32-P4 subsystem a pull request touches and then issuing follow-up calls with subsystem-specific questions—the control plane sends the primary Choice classification and all conditional Noul and Score questions in a single upfront request9. Because Jev evaluates all questions in parallel within roughly 100 ms and TypeSafe charges only per input token while output tokens are completely free, adding speculative questions incurs negligible latency and zero output token cost2. Once the response returns, deterministic application code checks the primary Choice answer and selectively reads only the relevant speculative answers while ignoring irrelevant branches9. Furthermore, when a commit modifies inline RISC-V assembly for Blake2b compression or secp256k1 scalar multiplication in a way that splits Jev's probability distribution across non-adjacent Score levels, the confidence \< 0.85 gate intercepts the bimodal uncertainty and routes the diff to the System Two LLM, while asymmetric Noul thresholds (noul \< 0.20 to pass, 0.20 \<= noul \<= 0.75 to escalate, and noul \> 0.75 to block) ensure that high-certainty vulnerabilities fail immediately without wasting System Two inference tokens2.

## **Integration One: Speculative Fan-Out PR Gatekeeper for Stateless SPM and Constant-Time Blake2b/Bitcoin Boundaries**

### **Mechanism and Architectural Justification**

The highest-impact integration deploys a synchronous **Speculative Fan-Out Gatekeeper** on every pull request modifying Rust source files (\*.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock)9. In a dual-mode (stateless and optionally stateful) ESP32-P4 Bitcoin Blake2b hardware wallet, the paramount software invariant is the strict isolation between **stateless ephemeral memory** and **stateful or external bus memory**4. When operating in Stateless Mode, the device derives master entropy and Blake2b-512 / HMAC-SHA512 key trees from an air-gapped QR seed or keypad input and must pin those secret structures strictly inside the ESP32-P4's internal **8 KB Scratchpad Memory (SPM)** or **32 KB LP SRAM**4. Stateless secrets must never be heap-allocated in external 16 MB or 32 MB Octal PSRAM (Vec, Box, String), must never be written to Non-Volatile Storage (NVS) flash partitions, must never pass through Debug or serial formatting macros, and must be zeroized immediately via ZeroizeOnDrop once the secp256k1 transaction signature is produced4. Simultaneously, because Blake2b and secp256k1 execute in Rust on the 400 MHz RISC-V HP cores rather than inside dedicated hardware state machines, any secret-dependent branching (if/else, match, or early-exit comparisons on private scalars, nonces, or intermediate digests) introduces timing and electromagnetic side-channel vulnerabilities4.  
Standard compiler checks (cargo clippy) cannot reliably determine whether a refactored struct containing a derived Blake2b subkey crosses the stateless-to-stateful boundary or introduces subtle variable-time branches. By packaging the git diff, changed file manifest, and architectural invariants into a structured JSON state object, a single Jev POST /v1/systemone request evaluates the subsystem Choice alongside atomic Noul and Score questions in parallel, escalating to the System Two LLM only when Jev's confidence drops below 0.85 or a Noul violation probability falls into the 0.20 to 0.75 uncertainty band2.

### **Exact Implementation in the esp32p4 Repository**

The repository implementation begins by establishing explicit hardware memory-section anchors in crates/wallet-core/src/stateless.rs so that both the Rust linker and Jev's semantic evaluation have unambiguous structural boundaries for stateless secrets on the ESP32-P4:

Rust  
\#\!\[no\_std\]  
use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};  
use blake2::{Blake2b512, Digest};

/// Forces allocation into the ESP32-P4 8 KB Scratchpad Memory (SPM)  
/// Never mapped to external Octal PSRAM or Flash cache.  
\#\[link\_section \= ".spm.stateless\_vault"\]  
\#\[repr(C, align(16))\]  
\#\[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)\]  
pub struct StatelessSeedVault {  
    master\_entropy: \[u8; 64\],  
    blake2b\_chain\_code: \[u8; 32\],  
    active\_session: bool,  
}

impl StatelessSeedVault {  
    \#\[inline(never)\]  
    pub fn derive\_blake2b\_subkey(&self, context: &\[u8\], index: u32) \-\> \[u8; 32\] {  
        let mut hasher \= Blake2b512::new();  
        hasher.update(&self.master\_entropy);  
        hasher.update(&self.blake2b\_chain\_code);  
        hasher.update(context);  
        hasher.update(\&index.to\_le\_bytes());  
        let digest \= hasher.finalize();  
        let mut subkey \= \[0u8; 32\];  
        // Constant-time copy without heap allocation  
        subkey.copy\_from\_slice(\&digest\[..32\]);  
        subkey  
    }  
}

Next, the repository integrates .github/scripts/jev\_pr\_gate.py to query https\://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone using the pinned model identifier jev-1.14 so that confidence thresholds remain stable across model releases3:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
import json  
import os  
import subprocess  
import sys  
import urllib.request

TYPESAFE\_API\_URL \= "https\://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone"  
PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL \= "jev-1.14"

def get\_pr\_diff\_state() \-\> dict:  
    base\_ref \= os.environ.get("GITHUB\_BASE\_REF", "main")  
    diff\_text \= subprocess.check\_output(  
        \["git", "diff", f"origin/{base\_ref}...HEAD", "--", "\*.rs", "Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"\],  
        text=True,  
    )  
    changed\_files \= subprocess.check\_output(  
        \["git", "diff", "--name-only", f"origin/{base\_ref}...HEAD"\],  
        text=True,  
    ).splitlines()  
    return {  
        "repository": "esp32p4-btc-blake2b-wallet",  
        "hardware\_target": "ESP32-P4 (Dual-Core 400MHz RISC-V HP, 40MHz LP, No Radio, 8KB SPM)",  
        "architecture\_invariants": \[  
            "Stateless mode secrets MUST reside in .spm.stateless\_vault or LP SRAM and implement ZeroizeOnDrop.",  
            "Stateless secrets MUST NEVER touch external PSRAM (vec/box heap), NVS flash, or serial log macros.",  
            "Blake2b and secp256k1 scalar/digest operations MUST execute in constant time without secret-dependent branching.",  
            "Stateful mode flash writes MUST pass through XTS-AES-256 encrypted partitions and hardware HMAC/DS wrappers."  
        \],  
        "changed\_files": changed\_files,  
        "git\_diff": diff\_text\[:45000\]  
    }

def call\_jev\_system\_one(state: dict) \-\> dict:  
    payload \= {  
        "model": PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL,  
        "state": state,  
        "questions": {  
            "primary\_subsystem": {  
                "type": "choice",  
                "instructions": "Which ESP32-P4 wallet subsystem is primarily modified by this pull request diff?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "stateless\_spm\_crypto": "Changes to Blake2b hashing, secp256k1 signing, BIP39/seed handling, or 8KB SPM memory buffers.",  
                    "stateful\_flash\_efuse": "Changes to NVS storage, XTS-AES flash partitions, eFuse OTP reads/writes, or key wrapping.",  
                    "airgap\_mipi\_hmi": "Changes to MIPI-CSI QR camera decoding, MIPI-DSI display rendering, or 2D-PPA UI graphics.",  
                    "non\_security\_support": "Changes restricted to documentation, non-crypto formatting, or host-side tooling."  
                }  
            },  
            "leaks\_stateless\_secret": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the code diff risk copying, heap-allocating, logging, or persisting stateless seed or Blake2b key material outside the 8KB SPM or without ZeroizeOnDrop?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "Secret arrays, seeds, or Blake2b subkeys are cloned to heap (Vec/Box/String), formatted with Debug/Display, logged via defmt/println, or written to NVS/flash during a stateless session.",  
                    "false": "All secret material remains stack-allocated or pinned to .spm.stateless\_vault, implements ZeroizeOnDrop, and never touches external PSRAM or logs."  
                }  
            },  
            "violates\_constant\_time": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the diff introduce secret-dependent branches, early-exit comparisons, or variable-time table lookups in Blake2b or Bitcoin secp256k1 paths?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "Uses standard \==, \!=, if/else, or match statements on secret scalars, nonces, or intermediate Blake2b/HMAC digests instead of constant-time subtle::ConstantTimeEq.",  
                    "false": "All cryptographic comparisons and conditional selects use constant-time primitives."  
                }  
            },  
            "exposes\_dma\_or\_external\_bus": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the diff pass unencrypted secret buffers to DMA controllers, USB OTG, SDIO, or external SPI/Octal PSRAM interfaces?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "Pointers to private keys, seeds, or unwrapped state are handed to DMA descriptors or peripheral TX buffers.",  
                    "false": "Only public keys, xpubs, or signed PSBT digests cross peripheral or DMA boundaries."  
                }  
            },  
            "crypto\_side\_channel\_severity": {  
                "type": "score",  
                "instructions": "Rate the cryptographic and memory-isolation risk introduced by this Rust diff.",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "0": "Strictly safe: Pure constant-time semantics, explicit ZeroizeOnDrop, and strict SPM memory isolation.",  
                    "1": "Moderate ambiguity: Complex lifetime refactoring, unsafe blocks, or inline RISC-V assembly that requires formal verification to confirm constant-time execution.",  
                    "2": "Critical vulnerability: Direct secret leakage, missing zeroization, or obvious secret-dependent branching."  
                }  
            }  
        }  
    }

    req \= urllib.request.Request(  
        TYPESAFE\_API\_URL,  
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),  
        headers={  
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ\['TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY'\]}",  
            "Content-Type": "application/json"  
        },  
        method="POST"  
    )  
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:  
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))

def escalate\_to\_system\_two\_llm(state: dict, jev\_answers: dict, reason: str) \-\> int:  
    print(f"::warning::\[ESCALATION TO SYSTEM 2 LLM\] Reason: {reason}")  
    audit\_context \= {  
        "escalation\_trigger": reason,  
        "jev\_calibrated\_telemetry": jev\_answers,  
        "focus\_instructions": (  
            "Perform a formal cryptographic and RISC-V RV32IMAFC assembly side-channel audit "  
            "on the provided diff. Focus specifically on the high-entropy/low-confidence signals "  
            "flagged by Jev System One."  
        )  
    }  
    with open("system2\_escalation\_payload.json", "w") as f:  
        json.dump(audit\_context, f, indent=2)  
    return 2

def main() \-\> int:  
    state \= get\_pr\_diff\_state()  
    if not state\["git\_diff"\].strip():  
        print("No Rust cryptographic files modified. Skipping gate.")  
        return 0

    response \= call\_jev\_system\_one(state)  
    ans \= response\["answers"\]  
    print(f"Evaluated by Jev model version: {response.get('model')}")

    domain \= ans\["primary\_subsystem"\]\["choice"\]  
    domain\_conf \= ans\["primary\_subsystem"\]\["confidence"\]  
    leak\_noul \= ans\["leaks\_stateless\_secret"\]\["noul"\]  
    ct\_noul \= ans\["violates\_constant\_time"\]\["noul"\]  
    dma\_noul \= ans\["exposes\_dma\_or\_external\_bus"\]\["noul"\]  
    sev\_score \= ans\["crypto\_side\_channel\_severity"\]\["score"\]  
    sev\_conf \= ans\["crypto\_side\_channel\_severity"\]\["confidence"\]

    \# 1\. Immediate Deterministic Hard Block on High-Probability Violations  
    if leak\_noul \> 0.75 or ct\_noul \> 0.75 or dma\_noul \> 0.75 or (sev\_score \>= 1.5 and sev\_conf \>= 0.80):  
        print(f"::error::\[JEV HARD BLOCK\] High-probability security violation detected: "  
              f"leak={leak\_noul:.2f}, const\_time={ct\_noul:.2f}, dma={dma\_noul:.2f}, score={sev\_score:.2f}")  
        return 1

    \# 2\. Speculative Fan-Out \+ Confidence-Gated Escalation to System 2 LLM  
    if domain\_conf \< 0.80:  
        return escalate\_to\_system\_two\_llm(state, ans, f"Subsystem classification confidence too low ({domain\_conf:.2f})")

    if domain in ("stateless\_spm\_crypto", "stateful\_flash\_efuse"):  
        if 0.20 \<= leak\_noul \<= 0.75 or 0.20 \<= ct\_noul \<= 0.75 or sev\_conf \< 0.85 or sev\_score \>= 0.65:  
            return escalate\_to\_system\_two\_llm(  
                state, ans,  
                f"Ambiguous crypto/memory signal in {domain} (score={sev\_score:.2f}, conf={sev\_conf:.2f})"  
            )

    print(f"\[JEV AUTO-PASS\] Domain={domain} (conf={domain\_conf:.2f}), Risk Score={sev\_score:.2f} (conf={sev\_conf:.2f})")  
    return 0

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    sys.exit(main())

## **Integration Two: Atomic Decomposition and Composite Scoring for ESP32-P4 eFuse, Flash Encryption, and Anti-Rollback Invariants**

### **Mechanism and Architectural Justification**

Even if the Rust source code is free of side channels, a modification to sdkconfig.defaults, partitions.csv, or build.rs can silently dismantle the ESP32-P4's **Optionally Stateful Mode** and hardware root of trust5. When a user opts into stateful seed storage on the ESP32-P4, physical security depends on five interdependent silicon and ESP-IDF bootloader configurations. Specifically, firmware authenticity requires **Secure Boot v2** using RSA-3072 or ECDSA (P-256/P-384) signatures anchored in eFuse OTP (CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT, CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_ENABLE\_AGGRESSIVE\_KEY\_REVOKE, and CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_V2\_ALLOW\_EFUSE\_RD\_DIS), while persistent secret confidentiality requires hardware **XTS-AES-256 Flash Encryption** (CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_ENC\_ENABLED and CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_CHECK\_ENC\_EN\_IN\_APP)7. Furthermore, to prevent downgrade attacks where an adversary flashes an older signed firmware image to extract stateful secrets, **Anti-Rollback protection** (CONFIG\_BOOTLOADER\_APP\_ANTI\_ROLLBACK) enforces a monotonic secure\_version counter in eFuse (configurable from 1 to 16 bits) and mandates an ota\_0 \+ ota\_1 partition scheme without an unverified factory partition8. At the same time, production configurations must never enable virtual eFuse simulation (EFUSE\_VIRTUAL, EFUSE\_VIRTUAL\_KEEP\_IN\_FLASH, or an emul\_efuse partition of size 0x2000) and must keep all cache-mapped executable app and OTA partitions strictly below the ESP32-P4's **16 MB (0x1000000) Quad-SPI cache mapping limit** unless experimental 32-bit cache addressing is explicitly managed7.  
As highlighted in TypeSafe's engineering documentation, asking a broad question ("Is this ESP-IDF configuration secure?") hides multiple distinct judgments behind a single uncalibrated output2. Integration Two therefore decomposes hardware configuration auditing into **five atomic Noul questions** and **one rubric Score**, combining the independent probabilities in deterministic code into a weighted **Composite Hardware Security Score**2.

| Atomic Question ID (POST /v1/systemone) | Primitive Type | ESP32-P4 Hardware / Kconfig Target Audited | Composite Weight (wiw\_iwi​) | Hard-Fail Threshold |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| weakens\_secure\_boot\_v2 | Noul | CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT, CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_INSECURE, CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_ENABLE\_AGGRESSIVE\_KEY\_REVOKE, CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_V2\_ALLOW\_EFUSE\_RD\_DIS8. | ![][image13] | noul \> 0.50 |
| weakens\_xts\_aes\_flash\_enc | Noul | CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_ENC\_ENABLED, CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_CHECK\_ENC\_EN\_IN\_APP, CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_PSEUDO\_ROUND\_FUNC8. | ![][image13] | noul \> 0.50 |
| compromises\_anti\_rollback | Noul | CONFIG\_BOOTLOADER\_APP\_ANTI\_ROLLBACK, secure\_version decrement, or presence of factory partition alongside ota\_0/ota\_18. | ![][image14] | noul \> 0.50 |
| leaks\_virtual\_efuse\_or\_jtag | Noul | EFUSE\_VIRTUAL, EFUSE\_VIRTUAL\_KEEP\_IN\_FLASH, emul\_efuse (0x2000) in production partition table, or insecure CONFIG\_SECURE\_UART\_ROM\_DL\_MODE8. | ![][image14] | noul \> 0.35 |
| violates\_16mb\_xip\_cache\_limit | Noul | App or OTA executable partitions placed at or above 0x1000000 (16 MB) in partitions.csv7. | ![][image15] | noul \> 0.60 |
| boot\_chain\_integrity\_rubric | Score (0–3) | Overall production readiness of the ESP-IDF bootloader, PMP/PMS permissions, and eFuse key-purpose allocation4. | Confidence Gate | score \> 0.50 or confidence \< 0.85 |

### **Exact Implementation in the esp32p4 Repository**

The repository implements .github/scripts/jev\_hw\_config\_gate.py to evaluate sdkconfig.defaults, partitions.csv, and build.rs whenever configuration files change:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
import json  
import os  
import sys  
import urllib.request

TYPESAFE\_API\_URL \= "https\://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone"  
PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL \= "jev-1.14"

def load\_file\_safe(path: str) \-\> str:  
    return open(path, "r").read() if os.path.exists(path) else ""

def evaluate\_hardware\_config() \-\> int:  
    state \= {  
        "sdkconfig\_defaults": load\_file\_safe("sdkconfig.defaults"),  
        "partitions\_production": load\_file\_safe("partitions.csv"),  
        "build\_rs": load\_file\_safe("build.rs"),  
        "mandatory\_production\_policy": {  
            "secure\_boot": "CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT=y, ECDSA P-256/P-384 or RSA-3072, aggressive revoke enabled, no CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_INSECURE.",  
            "flash\_encryption": "CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_ENC\_ENABLED=y (XTS-AES-256), CONFIG\_SECURE\_FLASH\_CHECK\_ENC\_EN\_IN\_APP=y.",  
            "anti\_rollback": "CONFIG\_BOOTLOADER\_APP\_ANTI\_ROLLBACK=y, secure\_version monotonic (1..16 bits), ota\_0 \+ ota\_1 without factory partition.",  
            "efuse\_and\_debug": "EFUSE\_VIRTUAL and emul\_efuse (0x2000) strictly forbidden in production sdkconfig.defaults and partitions.csv. UART ROM download locked to Secure mode.",  
            "memory\_map": "App and OTA executable partitions must remain strictly below 16MB (0x1000000) for Quad SPI XIP cache mapping."  
        }  
    }

    payload \= {  
        "model": PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL,  
        "state": state,  
        "questions": {  
            "weakens\_secure\_boot\_v2": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the configuration disable, bypass, or weaken Secure Boot v2 or eFuse read-protection of signing digests?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT is missing/disabled, CONFIG\_SECURE\_BOOT\_INSECURE is enabled, or aggressive key revoke is disabled.",  
                    "false": "Secure Boot v2 is strictly enforced with aggressive key revocation and eFuse read protection."  
                }  
            },  
            "weakens\_xts\_aes\_flash\_enc": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the configuration weaken XTS-AES Flash Encryption or allow unencrypted runtime execution?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "Flash encryption is disabled, release mode is missing, or app-level encryption check is disabled.",  
                    "false": "Flash encryption and in-app verification are strictly enabled."  
                }  
            },  
            "compromises\_anti\_rollback": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the configuration weaken eFuse anti-rollback protection or include an unverified factory partition alongside OTA partitions?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "CONFIG\_BOOTLOADER\_APP\_ANTI\_ROLLBACK is off, secure\_version is decreased, or partitions.csv includes a factory app partition.",  
                    "false": "Anti-rollback is enabled with monotonic secure\_version and an ota\_0 \+ ota\_1 only app partition layout."  
                }  
            },  
            "leaks\_virtual\_efuse\_or\_jtag": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the production configuration enable EFUSE\_VIRTUAL, include an emul\_efuse partition, or leave UART ROM download/JTAG unlocked?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "EFUSE\_VIRTUAL or EFUSE\_VIRTUAL\_KEEP\_IN\_FLASH is enabled, emul\_efuse (data, efuse, 0x2000) is present in partitions.csv, or ROM DL mode is unlocked.",  
                    "false": "Hardware eFuses are used exclusively and UART/JTAG debug interfaces are locked down."  
                }  
            },  
            "violates\_16mb\_xip\_cache\_limit": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Are any executable app or OTA partitions mapped at or above the 16MB (0x1000000) Quad SPI cache boundary?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "An app/ota partition offset \+ size reaches or exceeds 0x1000000 without explicit 32-bit cache mapping mitigation.",  
                    "false": "All executable app/ota partitions reside strictly below 0x1000000."  
                }  
            },  
            "boot\_chain\_integrity\_rubric": {  
                "type": "score",  
                "instructions": "Evaluate the overall hardware root-of-trust posture of the ESP32-P4 boot and partition configuration.",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "0": "Production hardened: All Secure Boot v2, XTS-AES-256, anti-rollback, JTAG lockdown, and \<16MB XIP constraints are satisfied.",  
                    "1": "Minor config drift: Non-critical diagnostic or log settings present that warrant review before release.",  
                    "2": "Degraded security: Development/emulation flags or partial encryption settings left enabled.",  
                    "3": "Broken root of trust: Unencrypted flash, virtual eFuses in production, or disabled anti-rollback."  
                }  
            }  
        }  
    }

    req \= urllib.request.Request(  
        TYPESAFE\_API\_URL,  
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),  
        headers={  
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ\['TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY'\]}",  
            "Content-Type": "application/json"  
        },  
        method="POST"  
    )  
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:  
        ans \= json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))\["answers"\]

    composite\_risk \= (  
        0.25 \* ans\["weakens\_secure\_boot\_v2"\]\["noul"\]  
        \+ 0.25 \* ans\["weakens\_xts\_aes\_flash\_enc"\]\["noul"\]  
        \+ 0.20 \* ans\["compromises\_anti\_rollback"\]\["noul"\]  
        \+ 0.20 \* ans\["leaks\_virtual\_efuse\_or\_jtag"\]\["noul"\]  
        \+ 0.10 \* ans\["violates\_16mb\_xip\_cache\_limit"\]\["noul"\]  
    )

    rubric\_score \= ans\["boot\_chain\_integrity\_rubric"\]\["score"\]  
    rubric\_conf \= ans\["boot\_chain\_integrity\_rubric"\]\["confidence"\]

    print(f"Hardware Composite Risk: {composite\_risk:.3f} \| Rubric Score: {rubric\_score:.2f} (conf={rubric\_conf:.2f})")

    if (  
        ans\["leaks\_virtual\_efuse\_or\_jtag"\]\["noul"\] \> 0.35  
        or composite\_risk \> 0.18  
        or rubric\_score \> 0.50  
    ):  
        print("::error::\[HARDWARE ROOT-OF-TRUST BLOCK\] ESP32-P4 security invariant violated.")  
        return 1

    if rubric\_conf \< 0.85 or composite\_risk \> 0.08:  
        print("::warning::\[ESCALATE TO SYSTEM 2 LLM & HARDWARE LEAD\] Ambiguous Kconfig/Partition modification.")  
        return 2

    return 0

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    sys.exit(evaluate\_hardware\_config())

## **Integration Three: Multimodal esp-emulator Air-Gap Verification and Framebuffer Spoofing Detection**

### **Mechanism and Architectural Justification**

An air-gapped Bitcoin hardware wallet depends on two runtime guarantees that static source analysis cannot verify alone: **What You See Is What You Sign (WYSIWYS)** on the physical display and **complete erasure of stateless secret material across processor resets**7. Because Espressif's Rust-based esp-emulator executes ESP32-P4 RISC-V firmware binaries directly—modeling the CPU, memory, flash encryption, and ECDSA (P-256/P-384) peripherals while preserving continuous flash state across simulated processor resets under pytest-embedded—the GitHub control plane can run end-to-end transaction signing and warm-reset cycles on every pull request7.  
During these esp-emulator runs, deterministic assertions struggle with visual layout verification and semantic trace inspection. When the firmware decodes an air-gapped Bitcoin PSBT and Blake2b commitment digest and renders the confirmation screen onto the MIPI-DSI framebuffer via the 2D-PPA graphics engine, brittle pixel-hash comparisons fail whenever font rendering or padding shifts, yet a UI regression that clips the tail characters of a bc1p Taproot address or obscures the transaction fee creates a severe spoofing vulnerability10. Simultaneously, because esp-emulator carries flash contents across resets in memory just like physical silicon, the control plane must verify that stateless sessions never write residue to flash or leave unzeroized entropy in .spm.stateless\_vault across a reset7. By enabling TypeSafe's multimodal image asset capability (TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true), the control plane passes the rendered MIPI-DSI confirmation PNG and a golden reference PNG in the assets dictionary (keyed by per-image UUID placeholders) alongside the esp-emulator reset trace in state6. In accordance with TypeSafe's API constraints, every UUID placeholder declared in assets must be referenced at least once in state, instructions, or criteria (or the endpoint returns HTTP 400), and each reference placement inserts a copy of the image into the model's context budget20.

### **Exact Implementation in the esp32p4 Repository**

The repository implements .github/scripts/jev\_emulator\_verify.py to evaluate both the esp-emulator post-reset trace and the rendered MIPI-DSI confirmation framebuffer against a golden reference image:

Python  
\#\!/usr/bin/env python3  
import base64  
import json  
import os  
import sys  
import uuid  
import urllib.request

TYPESAFE\_API\_URL \= "https\://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone"  
PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL \= "jev-1.14"

def encode\_png\_asset(filepath: str) \-\> dict:  
    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:  
        b64\_bytes \= base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("ascii")  
    return {  
        "type": "image",  
        "format": "png",  
        "data\_base64": b64\_bytes  
    }

def verify\_emulator\_run(trace\_log\_path: str, rendered\_ui\_png: str, golden\_ui\_png: str) \-\> int:  
    rendered\_ref \= f"asset-ui-{uuid.uuid4()}"  
    golden\_ref \= f"asset-golden-{uuid.uuid4()}"

    with open(trace\_log\_path, "r") as f:  
        emulator\_trace \= f.read()

    state \= {  
        "test\_vector": {  
            "mode": "Stateless Session \-\> Warm Reset \-\> Post-Reset Flash Inspection",  
            "expected\_btc\_recipient": "bc1p5d7rjq7g6rdk2yhzks9smlaqtedr4dekq08ge8ztwac72sfr9rusxg3297",  
            "expected\_amount\_sats": "14500000",  
            "expected\_fee\_sats": "12500",  
            "expected\_blake2b\_commitment\_prefix": "7f83b1657ff1fc53b92dc18148a1d65d"  
        },  
        "esp\_emulator\_serial\_and\_reset\_trace": emulator\_trace\[-20000:\],  
        "mipi\_dsi\_framebuffer\_capture": rendered\_ref  
    }

    payload \= {  
        "model": PINNED\_JEV\_MODEL,  
        "state": state,  
        "assets": {  
            rendered\_ref: encode\_png\_asset(rendered\_ui\_png),  
            golden\_ref: encode\_png\_asset(golden\_ui\_png)  
        },  
        "questions": {  
            "wysiwys\_display\_matches\_tx": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": (  
                    "Does the MIPI-DSI framebuffer capture accurately and legibly display the full "  
                    "expected Bitcoin Taproot recipient address, the exact amount (14,500,000 sats / 0.145 BTC), "  
                    "the fee, and the Blake2b commitment prefix without visual truncation or spoofing?"  
                ),  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": {  
                        "description": "Address, amount, fee, and Blake2b commitment are completely visible, unclipped, and match the layout clarity of the golden reference.",  
                        "examples": \[golden\_ref\]  
                    },  
                    "false": "Characters of the Bitcoin address or Blake2b commitment are clipped, obscured, mismatched with expected\_btc\_recipient, or visually ambiguous."  
                }  
            },  
            "stateless\_reset\_residue\_detected": {  
                "type": "noul",  
                "instructions": "Does the esp-emulator reset trace indicate that any seed entropy, Blake2b subkey, or session state survived in flash or unzeroized RAM after the processor reset?",  
                "criteria": {  
                    "true": "Post-reset memory or flash inspection logs show non-zero residue in .spm.stateless\_vault or unexpected NVS sector writes during a stateless session.",  
                    "false": "The .spm.stateless\_vault buffer is verified zeroized before reset and zero flash writes occurred during the stateless signing flow."  
                }  
            }  
        }  
    }

    req \= urllib.request.Request(  
        TYPESAFE\_API\_URL,  
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),  
        headers={  
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ\['TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY'\]}",  
            "Content-Type": "application/json",  
            "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images": "true"  
        },  
        method="POST"  
    )  
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=15) as resp:  
        ans \= json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))\["answers"\]

    wysiwys\_prob \= ans\["wysiwys\_display\_matches\_tx"\]\["noul"\]  
    residue\_prob \= ans\["stateless\_reset\_residue\_detected"\]\["noul"\]  
    print(f"Emulator Multimodal Audit \-\> WYSIWYS Match: {wysiwys\_prob:.2f} \| Stateless Residue Risk: {residue\_prob:.2f}")

    if wysiwys\_prob \< 0.85 or residue\_prob \> 0.15:  
        print("::error::\[EMULATOR AIR-GAP / STATELESS VERIFICATION FAILED\] UI mismatch or post-reset residue detected.")  
        return 1

    return 0

if \_\_name\_\_ \== "\_\_main\_\_":  
    sys.exit(verify\_emulator\_run(sys.argv\[1\], sys.argv\[2\], sys.argv\[3\]))

To orchestrate all three integrations within the GitHub control plane, the repository defines .github/workflows/jev\_control\_plane.yml. This workflow executes the deterministic Rust build, the esp-emulator test suite, and all three Jev System One gates on every pull request, triggering the secondary system\_two\_deep\_crypto\_audit job only when a confidence gate or middle-zone probability exits with code 2:

YAML  
name: ESP32-P4 Hybrid Jev \+ LLM Security Control Plane

on:  
  pull\_request:  
    branches: \[ main, release/\* \]

permissions:  
  contents: read  
  pull-requests: write

jobs:  
  system\_one\_jev\_gate:  
    name: Layer 1 \- Jev System One Fast Triage & Emulator Audit  
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest  
    outputs:  
      needs\_system\_two\_audit: \${{ steps.gate\_eval.outputs.escalate }}  
    steps:  
      \- name: Checkout ESP32-P4 Wallet Repository  
        uses: actions/checkout@v4  
        with:  
          fetch-depth: 0

      \- name: Run Integration 1 \- Speculative Fan-Out Rust Crypto & SPM Gate  
        id: int1  
        continue-on-error: true  
        env:  
          TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY: \${{ secrets.TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY }}  
          GITHUB\_BASE\_REF: \${{ github.base\_ref }}  
        run: python3 .github/scripts/jev\_pr\_gate.py

      \- name: Run Integration 2 \- ESP32-P4 eFuse & Flash Encryption Composite Gate  
        id: int2  
        continue-on-error: true  
        env:  
          TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY: \${{ secrets.TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY }}  
        run: python3 .github/scripts/jev\_hw\_config\_gate.py

      \- name: Build ESP32-P4 RISC-V Firmware & Execute esp-emulator Reset Suite  
        run: \|  
          cargo build \--release \--target riscv32imafc-unknown-none-elf  
          pytest \--embedded-services esp,idf tests/emulator\_stateless\_and\_airgap.py

      \- name: Run Integration 3 \- Multimodal esp-emulator Framebuffer & Residue Audit  
        id: int3  
        env:  
          TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY: \${{ secrets.TYPESAFE\_API\_KEY }}  
        run: \|  
          python3 .github/scripts/jev\_emulator\_verify.py \\  
            artifacts/emulator\_reset\_trace.log \\  
            artifacts/mipi\_dsi\_sign\_confirm.png \\  
            tests/golden/mipi\_dsi\_sign\_confirm\_golden.png

      \- name: Evaluate Deterministic Routing & Confidence Gates  
        id: gate\_eval  
        run: \|  
          if \[ "$steps.int1.outcome"=="failure"]||["${{ steps.int2.outcome }}" \== "failure" \]; then  
            if \[ \-f "system2\_escalation\_payload.json" \]; then  
              echo "escalate=true" \>\> \$GITHUB\_OUTPUT  
              exit 0  
            fi  
            echo "::error::Deterministic hard block triggered by Jev System One."  
            exit 1  
          fi  
          echo "escalate=false" \>\> \$GITHUB\_OUTPUT

      \- name: Upload Escalation Telemetry for System 2 LLM  
        if: steps.gate\_eval.outputs.escalate \== 'true'  
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4  
        with:  
          name: jev-escalation-context  
          path: system2\_escalation\_payload.json

  system\_two\_deep\_crypto\_audit:  
    name: Layer 2 \- Confidence-Gated System Two LLM Formal Audit  
    needs: system\_one\_jev\_gate  
    if: needs.system\_one\_jev\_gate.outputs.needs\_system\_two\_audit \== 'true'  
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest  
    steps:  
      \- uses: actions/checkout@v4  
        with:  
          fetch-depth: 0  
      \- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4  
        with:  
          name: jev-escalation-context  
      \- name: Run System Two Reasoning Model on Jev-Flagged Ambiguity  
        env:  
          REASONING\_LLM\_API\_KEY: \${{ secrets.REASONING\_LLM\_API\_KEY }}  
          GH\_TOKEN: \${{ secrets.GITHUB\_TOKEN }}  
        run: python3 .github/scripts/run\_system2\_crypto\_audit.py system2\_escalation\_payload.json

## **Prioritized Implementation Roadmap and High-Assurance Governance Conclusions**

Deploying Jev alongside a System Two reasoning model in the esp32p4 GitHub control plane achieves high-assurance cryptographic governance because it aligns each AI architecture with its mathematical strengths: deterministic code enforces control flow and threshold arithmetic, Jev (jev-1.14) delivers \~100 ms calibrated probability and confidence vectors across parallel atomic questions, and the System Two reasoning LLM is reserved strictly for low-confidence or ambiguous cryptographic modifications1. To maintain deterministic reliability over the repository lifecycle, the engineering workflow must enforce explicit model version pinning—sending jev-1.14 rather than the moving alias jev-latest and logging the returned model identifier on every CI run—because confidence gates (0.85) and composite risk weights are empirically tuned against a specific release's calibration curve3.  
In terms of rollout sequencing under tight development schedules, the repository should implement **Integration One** (Speculative Fan-Out PR Gatekeeper for .spm.stateless\_vault isolation and constant-time Blake2b/secp256k1 execution) first, as it protects core cryptographic development from day one4. **Integration Two** (Atomic Decomposition and Composite Scoring for Secure Boot v2, XTS-AES-256 flash encryption, anti-rollback secure\_version counters, and the 16 MB Quad-SPI XIP boundary) should follow immediately as stateful NVS/flash storage and partition tables are finalized7. Finally, **Integration Three** (Multimodal esp-emulator framebuffer WYSIWYS verification and warm-reset residue auditing) completes the verification loop once the MIPI-CSI/DSI optical QR transport layer is integrated6. Because TypeSafe never trains Jev on customer requests or responses and offers Zero Data Retention (ZDR), the hardware wallet repository preserves strict intellectual property and security confidentiality across all automated control plane audits3.
